B7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Nothing here is functional. Whether a coherent feedforward loop actually delays a
response, or a negative feedback actually speeds one, needs perturbation time-course
data that is not on this disk, and this loop does not gesture at those claims.
CollecTRI is literature-curated, so its edges are enriched for the interactions
people looked for. A motif can be over-represented because it is over-studied, and
no degree-preserving null can see that.
The double-edge swap preserves in-degree and out-degree exactly but not higher-order
structure, so an enrichment could still reflect modularity rather than circuitry.
Signs are Activation/Repression/Unknown as curated; a context-dependent factor that
activates in one setting and represses in another is recorded as one or the other.
B6's null is a configuration model sampled by stub matching, which permits multi-
edges, so it compares a simple observed graph against a multigraph ensemble. For a
rare-event count that is the standard null, but it is not the same object.
And a curated self-loop needs someone to have specifically tested whether a factor
binds its own promoter. Holding out-degree and in-degree fixed controls for how much
a factor has been studied in general; it cannot control for whether THAT experiment
was the one somebody ran. B6 measures curation against chance, not biology against
chance, and a positive result would be consistent with either.
B3 compares two z-scores from two DIFFERENT graphs. Equalising the nulls removes one
confound and not the others: the tiers differ in density, in how signs were assigned
and in what an edge means, and a z-score is not a quantity those differences leave
alone. B3 is a direction-of-difference test and is not read as a ratio.
